findings.summary: The tick node body cannot actually invoke the tick entry as written. bin/deep-research-loop.sh:25 defaults TICK_ENTRY to the two-word string `bash "<root>/bin/tick-entry.sh"`, which renders into the fleet as a plain YAML scalar and is then substituted into `tick_entry="{{tick_entry}}"`; bash collapses that to the single word `bash <root>/bin/tick-entry.sh`, so `"$tick_entry" --selfcheck` looks up one command literally named `bash /.../tick-entry.sh` and fails with 127 under `set -e`. Unquoting the expansion, or setting TICK_ENTRY to the script path alone, fixes it. I do not charge this against the acceptance set: §3 rules that real execution is V1 and that this package proves only that the wiring exists and parses, §4's table (asserted complete against every ⛔ and qualifier) has no row that executes tick.md, and §5 has no matching mutation — no G row is broken. It is also inferred from the natural textual-substitution semantics of the engine's template renderer, which is not readable from this worktree. Recorded so V1 fixes it before the first real launch rather than discovering it there.

Nothing ever seeds the trigger store, so the assembled fleet would drive zero ticks on a real run. bin/deep-research-loop.sh:28 only `mkdir -p`s TRIGGER_STORE_DIR, and a repo-wide search finds no writer of any record into it; `pending.status: open` would therefore match nothing and `drain` would complete without running the tick pipeline. Even with a record present, `claim: {from: open, to: done}` retires it on first success, so `max_passes: 16` yields at most one tick rather than the repeated wake-up §1 assigns to loop-engine. This satisfies G2/G3/G5 as written (the store is genuinely trigger-only and carries no clue/board semantics, which is the ⛔ §1 was defending), and the package correctly does not claim a real run, but the '周期驱动' leg of §1 is expressed structurally without a producer behind it.

Neither of §1's other two loop-engine provisions is expressed in the fleet: there is no named-lock declaration for the `synthesizer` / `triage` singletons (spec §1 item 2, §3.6) and no crash-recovery/reclaim binding (item 3). §4 has no G row for either, and S2's reclaim step already implements card recovery on the bus side, so nothing in the acceptance set fails; the single `tick` pipeline is simply the minimal shape that satisfies G2-G5. Noted because a follow-up that assumes the lock wiring already exists in this fleet would be wrong.

Both delivered shell entry points are committed non-executable (mode 644 in the checked-out worktree) despite carrying `#!/usr/bin/env bash`, so `./bin/deep-research-loop.sh --dry-run` — the literal form G1 names — would fail with permission denied. Every in-repo caller invokes them through `bash` (package.json:18 `deep-research:dry-run`, test/plugin-wiring.test.ts:17 execFileSync("bash", ...), bin/tick-entry.sh via the same path), and the dev-note records the `bash bin/...` form, so G1/G6 pass as exercised. Setting the exec bit would make the shipped entry points match their shebangs.
